prompts: The investors meet tomorrow and want the first half of 2026 closed. The books and the board's notes are in {WS}/finance. How did each month go, and how many months of cash do we have left at the current burn? Prepare what the CFO needs to present. Record the key figures in {WS}/result.json: revenue, gross_margin_pct and ebitda, each mapping 2026-01 to 2026-06 to its value, plus burn and runway_months.
answers:
Result verified against computed values; the work is done — no browser or apps were opened to close.

**[goal]** Close H1 2026, show monthly performance and cash runway for the CFO deck, record key figures in `result.json`.

**[action]** Parsed `finance/` (README, chart of accounts, 86 ledger lines Jan–Jun 2026, closing cash balances) and computed each month's P&L from the ledger with a script, then wrote `result.json`.

**[result]** H1 2026 by month (R$, from ledger):

| Month | Revenue | Gross margin | EBITDA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-01 | 200,510.87 | 70.03% | −210,278.96 |
| 2026-02 | 216,328.06 | 70.29% | −212,300.08 |
| 2026-03 | 219,066.17 | 68.46% | −204,525.45 |
| 2026-04 | 238,163.26 | 70.24% | −196,950.65 |
| 2026-05 | 243,032.89 | 69.56% | −201,945.82 |
| 2026-06 | 272,391.57 | 72.41% | −192,968.22 |

Revenue grew ~36% over H1; gross margin held ~68–72%; EBITDA loss narrowed from ~−210k to ~−193k.
- **Burn (per board note in README):** average monthly negative EBITDA of last 3 closed months (Apr–Jun) = **197,288.23**
- **Runway:** 1,847,350.40 (30/06/2026 balance, `cash_balance.txt`) ÷ burn = **9.4 months**

**Assumptions stated:** EBITDA = gross profit + opex (sales_marketing, rnd, ga); financial items (6.1.01/6.1.02, ~±10k/mo) excluded per standard practice; refunds in 3.1.09 net against revenue; burn defined by the board's own rule in the README; cash is the latest closing balance (30/06).

**[next]** None — `result.json` is written with all requested keys.

**What I found and how I know it's right:** I found the ledger contains all H1 entries across the full account map (86 lines, all accounts mapped to P&L lines; the script would have raised on any unmapped account), the board's burn rule in the README, and two closing balances in `cash_balance.txt`. Computation was done in `python` (decimal arithmetic, no float drift in the math path), the printed monthly EBITDA values match the values written to `result.json`, and I re-read the JSON back to confirm the exact keys and values. The one judgment call — excluding financial income/expense from EBITDA — is the standard CFO definition; if the board wants financial items included, June's EBITDA would improve by ~5.6k and burn by ~1.2k/mo, which I can adjust in one line if asked.
